name: 01 - Direct Play Optimizer (Full Pipeline)
description: Full pipeline: HEVC/MP4 with stereo AAC 2.0 + EAC3 5.1 surround, hvc1 tag, faststart, resolution-tiered quality, NVENC GPU with software fallback, health check, duration validation, optional Plex/arr notifications. Configure via the top config variable nodes.

flowPlugins.name: Input File

── CONFIGURATION ─────────────────────────────
All user-configurable options are set here as
flow variables. Edit the VALUE field of each
'Set Variable' node below to configure:

  remove_commentary  (true/false)
    Remove director commentary, audio description,
    and hearing-impaired audio tracks.
    Default: true  ★ Opinionated — set false to keep.

  enable_plex_notify  (true/false)
    Trigger a Plex library refresh after each file
    is replaced. Requires Plex URL+token in the
    'Notify Plex' webRequest node near the bottom.
    Default: false  ★ Must configure URL+token first.

  enable_arr_notify  (true/false)
    Notify Radarr/Sonarr after file replacement.
    Requires API key in the 'Notify Arr' node.
    Default: false  ★ Must configure API key first.

Set Variable: remove_commentary
★ Change value to 'false' to keep commentary tracks

Set Variable: enable_plex_notify
★ Change value to 'true' after configuring
  the 'Notify Plex' node URL + token below

Set Variable: enable_arr_notify
★ Change value to 'true' after configuring
  the 'Notify Arr' node API key + host below

── GUARD CHECKS ──────────────────────────────
Skips files already optimal for direct play.
All 4 checks must pass to skip processing:

  1. Container is MP4 or M4V
  2. Video codec is HEVC
  3. Has at least one AAC audio stream
  4. Has at least one 2-channel (stereo) stream

Any failure → processing pipeline.
All pass → mark done (no re-encode).

GUARD 1 of 4 — Container is MP4/M4V?
★ CONFIGURE: add extensions as needed
GUARD 2 of 4 — Video codec is HEVC?
GUARD 3 of 4 — Has AAC audio stream?
GUARD 4 of 4 — Has 2-channel (stereo) stream?

✅ FILE ALREADY OPTIMAL
All guards passed. Marking as processed.

Replace Original File
(no-op: marks file done, nothing changed)

🔧 NEEDS PROCESSING
One or more guards failed. Running full pipeline.

── PRE-CHECK 1: LOW BITRATE SKIP ─────────────
Skips files with overall bitrate ≤ 1 Mbps.

Why: Very low-bitrate files are typically trailers,
extras, featurettes, or already heavily compressed
content. Re-encoding HEVC at very low bitrates:
  • Produces worse quality than the source
  • Wastes GPU encode sessions on tiny files
  • NVENC performs poorly near its quality floor

Output 1 (>1 Mbps): proceed to processing
Output 2 (≤1 Mbps): mark done without re-encoding

★ CONFIGURE: greaterThan=1 (Mbps)
  Increase to 2 or 3 to also skip low-res trailers.
  Delete this node and its comment to disable
  the skip and process ALL files regardless.

Check Overall Bitrate > 1 Mbps
★ Config: greaterThan=1 (Mbps) | lessThan=500

⏭ SKIP: Bitrate ≤ 1 Mbps
File too small/compressed to benefit from HEVC.
Marking as processed without changes.

Replace Original File
(no-op: low-bitrate skip, no changes made)

── PRE-CHECK 2: SOURCE FILE HEALTH CHECK ─────
Runs a quick integrity check on the source file
before spending GPU time encoding it.

Catches: corrupt containers, missing keyframes,
truncated files, unreadable streams.

type: 'quick' uses HandBrake --scan (fast, ~1s).
  If HandBrake is not in your Tdarr container,
  change to 'thorough' (uses FFmpeg, much slower).
type: 'thorough' does a full decode pass (minutes).

★ CONFIGURE: type = 'quick' or 'thorough'
  Delete this node and its comment to disable
  health checking entirely.

Health Check Source File
★ Config: type='quick' (HandBrake) or 'thorough' (FFmpeg)

── STEP 1: SET CONTAINER → MP4 ───────────────
forceConform=true auto-removes MP4-incompatible
streams: PGS image subtitles, attachments (fonts),
EIA-608, timed_id3, and mov_text data.

★ CONFIGURE: container = 'mp4' or 'mkv'
  forceConform = 'true' (recommended) or 'false'

Set Container → MP4
★ Config: container=mp4 | forceConform=true

── STEP 2: REMOVE ALL SUBTITLES ──────────────
Removes ALL subtitle streams for maximum direct
play compatibility.

Rationale: PGS/image subtitles always force
transcoding on iOS/Plex/web. Text subs (ASS/SRT)
cause transcoding on many clients. Removing all
subs is the safest option for direct play.

★ OPINIONATED — To keep text subtitles instead:
  1. Delete this comment and the RemoveSubtitles
     node below.
  2. Add RemoveStreamByProperty targeting:
     codec_name = hdmv_pgs_subtitle,pgssub,
     dvd_subtitle,dvb_subtitle,dvb_teletext
Remove All Subtitles

── STEP 3: COMMENTARY TRACK REMOVAL ─────────
Controlled by the 'remove_commentary' variable
set at the top of this flow.

★ Opt-in (default: true). To DISABLE:
  Change var_rm_commentary value to 'false'.

What gets removed (case-insensitive title match):
  • 'commentary' — director/cast commentary
  • 'description' — audio descriptions for blind
  • 'descriptive' — descriptive audio service
  • 'sdh' — subtitles for deaf/hard of hearing audio
  • 'hearing impaired' — hearing impaired audio
  • 'hearing-impaired' — alternate tag form

These tracks are common in Blu-ray rips and
typically never used by home media viewers.
Removing them saves space and reduces audio
track confusion in client players.

Check: remove_commentary == 'true'?
(YES → remove commentary tracks)
(NO  → skip, keep all audio tracks)

Remove Commentary/Description Audio Tracks
(matches by stream title tag, case-insensitive)
★ Edit valuesToRemove to add/remove patterns

── STEP 4: REMOVE DATA STREAMS ───────────────
Removes data streams (teletext, SCTE markers,
chapter data streams, broadcast metadata).
These are incompatible with MP4 and unused.
Remove Data Streams

── STEP 5: NVENC GPU AVAILABILITY CHECK ──────
Verifies NVIDIA NVENC (hevc_nvenc) is accessible
before attempting GPU encoding.

Output 1 (NVENC available):
  → Resolution-tiered NVENC encoding
  → Different QP per resolution for optimal
    quality/size ratio on T400

Output 2 (NVENC unavailable):
  → Software libx265 fallback at CRF 22
  → Much slower but same output format
  → Common causes: GPU sessions exhausted
    (T400 limit: 4 simultaneous), driver issue,
    container missing nvidia runtime

★ CONFIGURE: hardwareEncoder = 'hevc_nvenc'
  Change to 'hevc_qsv' for Intel QSV, etc.

Check: NVENC GPU Available?
★ Config: hardwareEncoder=hevc_nvenc

── STEP 5a: RESOLUTION-TIERED NVENC ENCODING ─
Different QP (Quantization Parameter) per
resolution tier for optimal quality/size balance.
T400 uses QP mode (not CRF like software x265).

  SD / 720p  →  QP 26  (looser compression OK;
                          content has less detail)
  1080p      →  QP 24  (sweet spot for HEVC/NVENC)
  1440p / 4K →  QP 28  (4K has more redundant data;
                          QP 28 still looks great;
                          avoids huge file sizes)
  Unknown    →  QP 24  (safe default)

All paths use:
  forceEncoding=false → stream-copy existing HEVC
  hardwareDecoding=true → NVDEC for decode
  preset=slow → NVENC p6 (best NVENC quality)

★ CONFIGURE: ffmpegQuality in each encoder node.
  Lower QP = better quality, larger file.
  NVENC recommended range: 20 (high) to 30 (small)

Check Video Resolution
(outputs 1-9: 480p, 576p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p,
4K UHD, DCI 4K, 8K, Other/Unknown)

NVENC Encoder — SD / 720p  (QP 26)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=26 (range 20-30)

NVENC Encoder — 1080p  (QP 24)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=24 (range 20-28)

NVENC Encoder — 4K / 1440p  (QP 28)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=28 (range 24-32)

── STEP 5b: SOFTWARE FALLBACK (no NVENC) ─────
NVENC was not available. Falling back to
software libx265 encoding.

Settings: CRF 22, preset slow.
CRF 22 for libx265 is approximately equivalent
to NVENC QP 24-26 in perceptual quality.

This will be significantly slower than GPU
encoding. Consider:
  • Reducing concurrent workers
  • Fixing NVENC availability (check docker runtime)
  • Increasing Tdarr worker timeout

★ CONFIGURE: ffmpegQuality = CRF value (18-28)

Software Encoder — libx265 CRF 22 (NVENC fallback)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=22 (CRF, range 18-28)

── STEP 6: HVC1 TAG + FASTSTART ──────────────
  -tag:v hvc1
    Required for iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS native HEVC
    hardware decoding. FFmpeg defaults to 'hev1'.
    Works with both stream-copy and re-encoded HEVC.

  -movflags +faststart
    Moves MP4 moov atom to file start for web
    streaming and Plex progressive download.

★ CONFIGURE: outputArguments field

Add hvc1 Tag + Faststart
★ outputArguments: -tag:v hvc1 -movflags +faststart

── STEP 7: AUDIO — STEREO AAC 2.0 ───────────
Adds stereo AAC 2.0 downmix if not present.
This is the universal fallback track that plays
on ALL clients without transcoding.

Two passes:
  eng: targets English-tagged audio streams
  und: targets untagged/undefined audio
  (add more nodes for other languages)

Plugin is idempotent: if 2ch AAC already exists,
it's a no-op. Won't add duplicates.

★ CONFIGURE:
  - bitrate: 192k (128k-256k reasonable)
  - language: 'eng' / 'und' (add more as needed)
  - channels: 2 (don't change for stereo)

Ensure Stereo AAC 2.0 — Pass 1 (lang: eng)
★ Config: bitrate=192k | channels=2 | lang=eng

Ensure Stereo AAC 2.0 — Pass 2 (lang: und)
★ Config: bitrate=192k | channels=2 | lang=und

── STEP 8: AUDIO — EAC3 5.1 SURROUND ────────
Adds Dolby Digital Plus (EAC3) 5.1 surround if
no EAC3 5.1 track exists. This replaces DTS as
the surround format (DTS is removed in Step 9).

Why EAC3 instead of keeping DTS:
  • DTS (dca) causes Plex to TRANSCODE on iOS
    even when stereo AAC is present as track 1
  • EAC3 is MP4-compatible and Plex iOS direct-plays
    it natively — no transcoding needed
  • AC3/EAC3 are the Dolby formats Apple devices
    support natively for surround

Two passes: eng and und (same as AAC stereo).
Plugin is idempotent — no-op if EAC3 5.1 exists.
Plugin creates 5.1 from the best available source
(DTS 7.1 → EAC3 5.1 downmix, TrueHD → EAC3 5.1).

Note: Files with existing AC3 5.1 will get an
additional EAC3 5.1 track. Both are kept (AC3
for legacy receiver compat). This is fine but
slightly redundant — add 'ac3' to Step 9 removal
list if you want to eliminate AC3 and keep EAC3 only.

★ OPINIONATED — To skip EAC3 conversion entirely
  and instead just remove DTS:
  1. Delete these two EnsureAudioStream nodes
     and their comment.
  2. Add 'dca' to valuesToRemove in Step 9.
  Result: files get AAC stereo only (no surround).

★ CONFIGURE:
  - bitrate: 384k (EAC3 5.1 recommended: 256k-640k)
  - channels: 6 (5.1). For 7.1 preservation, add
    two more nodes with channels=8.

Ensure EAC3 5.1 Surround — Pass 1 (lang: eng)
★ Config: bitrate=384k | channels=6 | lang=eng

Ensure EAC3 5.1 Surround — Pass 2 (lang: und)
★ Config: bitrate=384k | channels=6 | lang=und

── STEP 9: REMOVE INCOMPATIBLE AUDIO CODECS ──
Removes codecs that:
  a) Cannot be stored in MP4 containers, OR
  b) Cause client transcoding (now replaced by EAC3)

  REMOVED:
    truehd  - Dolby TrueHD/Atmos (not MP4-compatible;
              now replaced by EAC3 5.1 from Step 8)
    mlp     - Meridian Lossless Packing (TrueHD base)
    dca     - DTS/DTS-HD (causes iOS Plex transcoding;
              now replaced by EAC3 5.1 from Step 8)
    flac    - Lossless, not MP4-compatible
    vorbis  - Not standard in MP4
    opus    - Not standard in MP4
    wma/wmav2/wmapro - Windows Media (no value here)

  KEPT:
    aac   - Universal stereo (added in Step 7)
    eac3  - Dolby Digital Plus surround (added Step 8)
    ac3   - Dolby Digital (legacy compat, kept)
    mp3   - Legacy but widely compatible

★ CONFIGURE: Add 'ac3' to valuesToRemove if you
  want to keep ONLY EAC3+AAC (removes legacy AC3).

Remove Incompatible/Replaced Audio Codecs
(truehd,mlp,dca,flac,vorbis,opus,wma variants)
★ Add 'ac3' to also remove legacy Dolby Digital

── STEP 10: REORDER STREAMS ──────────────────
Final stream order:
  [0] Video (HEVC)
  [1] Stereo AAC 2.0  ← FIRST (universal compat)
  [2] EAC3 5.1        ← surround for capable clients
  [3] AC3 5.1         ← if originally present
  [4+] Any remaining text subtitles

Why stereo AAC first: video.js, basic iOS apps,
and many web players use the FIRST audio track.
Putting stereo AAC first ensures universal playback.

★ CONFIGURE:
  - channels: '2,6,8' = stereo before surround
  - codecs: 'aac,eac3,ac3,mp3' = preference order
  - languages: 'eng,und' = add your primary lang

Reorder Streams
(stereo AAC → EAC3 surround → AC3 → subtitles)
★ Config: channels=2,6,8 | codecs=aac,eac3,ac3,mp3

── STEP 11: EXECUTE FFMPEG ───────────────────
Runs the assembled FFmpeg command.
Output goes to Tdarr cache; validated before replace.
Execute FFmpeg Command

── STEP 12: VALIDATE OUTPUT FILE SIZE ─────────
Output must be within 0-120% of original size.
HEVC should almost always be smaller.
>120% indicates a problem (misconfigured QP,
already-compressed source, very short clip).

→ OK: proceed to duration check
→ FAIL: send to Review queue, keep original

★ CONFIGURE: lessThan = '120' (120% of original)
  Increase to 150 if you see false positives.

Validate: Output Size ≤ 120% of Original
★ Config: lessThan=120 | greaterThan=0

⚠ OUTPUT TOO LARGE (size check failed)
File exceeded 120% of original size.
Sending to Review. Original preserved.

Check: Tdarr → Files → Needs Review.
Common causes: very short clip, already-
compressed source, QP too low for content.
★ Fix: increase ffmpegQuality in encoder nodes.

── STEP 13: VALIDATE OUTPUT DURATION ─────────
Output duration must be within 98-102% of source.
Catches: truncated audio, dropped frames, corrupt
transcodes that pass the size check.

For stream-copy operations the duration should
be exactly 100% — any deviation is suspicious.
For re-encoded content, small rounding differences
(fractional frames) keep this within 99-101%.

→ OK: proceed to replace original
→ FAIL: send to Review queue, keep original

★ CONFIGURE: greaterThan=98, lessThan=102
  Widen to 95/105 if you have intentionally
  trimmed or padded content in your library.

Validate: Output Duration within 98-102% of Original
★ Config: greaterThan=98 | lessThan=102

⚠ DURATION MISMATCH (duration check failed)
Output duration deviates >2% from original.
Possible corrupt transcode. Original preserved.

Check: Tdarr → Files → Needs Review.
Inspect both files with ffprobe before deciding.

Flag for Review
(original preserved; check Needs Review queue)

── STEP 14: REPLACE ORIGINAL ─────────────────
Both validations passed. Replacing original file.
Replace Original File with Transcoded MP4

── STEP 15: POST-PROCESSING NOTIFICATIONS ────
Optional notifications after file replacement.
Controlled by variables set at the top of the flow.

Plex Notify (enable_plex_notify = 'true'):
  Triggers a Plex library refresh so Plex
  immediately picks up the new file/codec info.
  ★ Configure the 'Notify Plex' webRequest node:
    - Update the URL with your Plex server IP
    - Replace YOUR_PLEX_TOKEN with your token
    - Get your token: Plex Settings → Account
      → Privacy → 'Show' Plex Token

Radarr/Sonarr Notify (enable_arr_notify = 'true'):
  Notifies *arr to refresh metadata and check
  the file against its expected quality profile.
  ★ Configure the 'Notify Arr' node:
    - arr: 'radarr' or 'sonarr'
    - arr_host: your *arr URL
    - arr_api_key: Settings → General → API Key
  To notify BOTH Radarr and Sonarr, duplicate
  the 'Notify Arr' node and update each one.

Check: enable_plex_notify == 'true'?
(YES → send Plex refresh request)
(NO  → skip to arr check)

Notify Plex — Refresh Library
★ CONFIGURE: Update URL with your Plex IP + token
  URL format: http://PLEX_IP:32400/library/sections/all/refresh?X-Plex-Token=TOKEN
  method: GET

Check: enable_arr_notify == 'true'?
(YES → notify Radarr/Sonarr)
(NO  → done)

Notify Radarr/Sonarr
★ CONFIGURE:
  arr: 'radarr' or 'sonarr'
  arr_host: 'http://YOUR_IP:7878' (Radarr)
             'http://YOUR_IP:8989' (Sonarr)
  arr_api_key: Settings → General → API Key
  Duplicate this node to notify BOTH services.

── ERROR HANDLING ────────────────────────────
Global error handler — catches all unhandled
errors from any node in this flow.
Original file is NOT modified on error.
Reset Flow Error State

Fail Flow
(file marked as Error in Tdarr; original preserved)
